overview.headline: Origins and ratification of the Bill of Rights in 1791

keyPoints.point: 12 amendments were proposed and 10 ratified became the Bill of Rights
keyPoints.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyPoints.point: Opponents charged the drafted Constitution would open the way to tyranny
keyPoints.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny

keyPoints.point: State conventions asked for amendments during formal ratification of the Constitution
keyPoints.quote: Several state conventions in their formal ratification of the Constitution asked for such amendments

keyPoints.point: The First Congress proposed 12 amendments to meet arguments against the Constitution
keyPoints.quote: the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution

keyTerms.gloss: 10 ratified amendments defining citizens rights in relation to government
keyTerms.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyTerms.gloss: harsh rule by central government feared under drafted Constitution
keyTerms.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny

keyTerms.gloss: formal approval of the Constitution by state conventions
keyTerms.quote: Several state conventions in their formal ratification of the Constitution asked for such amendments

keyTerms.gloss: proposed changes to the Constitution considered by state legislatures
keyTerms.quote: the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution
